newsitem.title: GERMANY: North African countries buying soy, sun oil in Q4.
newsitem.headline: North African countries buying soy, sun oil in Q4.

text.p: Five North African countries would import more soy oil and sunflower oil and less rape oil in the fourth quarter of 1996 compared with the same period last year, basing decisions on prices, Oil World newsletter said.

It said they would buy a combined 170,000 tonnes of soy oil and 125,000 tonnes of sunflower oil in the period versus 135,000 and 81,000 tonnes respectively a year earlier. The countries are Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria, Egypt and Libya.
Rape oil purchases in Oct-Dec 1996 by the five were put at 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes versus 73,000 tonnes a year earlier, due to rape oil's price premium.
Rape oil purchases in July-September 1996 were already down at 16,000 tonnes from 44,000 in the same 1995 period.
Fourth quarter 1996 palm oil imports by the North African countries were seen slightly higher than in Oct-Dec 1995 at 105,000-110,000 tonnes (101,000 tonnes previously).
In remarks on the full 1996/97 season, Oil World said a higher olive oil crop in Tunisia would help reduce oils and fats import demand in that country and the whole region.
Palm oil imports were likely to rise in Jan-Sept 1997.
